title: UI Rollouts & Analytics Sync — Week of 2026-06-08
content:
Purpose: capture the cross-functional standup and follow-ups for UI rollouts, analytics gaps, and the A/B fallback run we executed on 2026-06-10. This is a synthesis (not a formal runbook) — notes, open questions, and next steps.

Quick summary:
- Canary on v3.4.1 (partial rollout to 5% traffic) triggered unexpected errors in the rollout telemetry pipeline, causing a 20% undercount of route-level latency metrics for ~90 minutes on 2026-06-10 03:10–04:40 UTC.
- Root cause appears to be a schema change in the frontend tracing payload that the aggregation job didn’t tolerate. We rolled back the canary at 03:35 and re-routed metrics ingestion to the legacy collector.
- Customer visible impact: none (UI feature guarded by feature flag), but internal dashboards were misleading which affected on-call decisioning.

Attendees (standup cadence: daily 09:30 PT during rollout week):
- Priya D. (owner) — console rollouts / runbook lead
- Ethan P. — frontend (feature implementation + telemetry payload)
- Marta L. — observability / dashboards
- Samir G. — backend ingestion / aggregation jobs
- Jordan K. — product rollout coordinator
- SRE on-call rotated in for incident minutes

Notes and per-person updates:
- Ethan: shipped the telemetry change to include a new field `renderPathV2` to support richer routing analytics. Forgot to update the aggregation schema in MET-3380. My bad — PR 892 has the frontend change. Reverting the telemetry change for the canary build today and adding a feature-flag gated payload.
- Samir: aggregation job assumed flat JSON keys; new nested path caused partial failures (silently dropped rows). We replayed the drop window from the event store and reprocessed; counts look consistent now but need a full verification over 24h. Open: add schema validation to ingestion and alert on dropped-row ratios above 0.5%.
- Marta: dashboards displayed 0% for route latency for several routes; investigated and found suppressed alerts due to a metrics tag mismatch. Restored visualizations after re-ingestion pipeline fix. Need to refresh dashboard caching TTL to avoid stale zeroes during re-ingest.
- Jordan: coordinated rollback; notified product owners and legal (internal memo) because enterprise customers had flagged increased monitoring noise. Recommend a formal pre-rollout checklist update to require ingestion schema sign-off.

Blockers and open questions:
- Who owns schema evolution policy for telemetry payloads? (Ethan + Samir collaborating; need product sign-off).
- How do we make rollouts resilient to partial analytics failures so on-call doesn't get blinded? Proposal below.
- Do we add a synthetic traffic job to verify both UI and telemetry end-to-end before canary? Cost estimate requested from infra.

Immediate actions (by priority):
1) Short term (next 24–48h):
   - Add a schema validation step in the aggregation job; block any unknown top-level keys from being dropped silently. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-06-15.
   - Re-run full re-ingest verification for the 2026-06-10 window and publish verification note. Owner: Marta + Samir. ETA: 2026-06-14.
   - Create a temporary dashboard flag that surfaces re-ingest in progress (red banner) so on-call knows to ignore transient zeros. Owner: Marta. ETA: 2026-06-13.

2) Mid term (2–4 weeks):
   - Pre-rollout telemetry contract: a short doc that lists allowed payload keys + required tags and a lightweight sign-off flow (owners: frontend + ingestion). Draft: Priya. ETA: 2026-06-26.
   - Integrate a lightweight synthetic test that exercises the end-to-end path (UI -> collector -> aggregation -> dashboard). Start as smoke test in staging. Owner: Ethan + Infra. ETA: 2026-07-02.
   - Dashboard caching TTL: reduce to 2 min for rollout-critical dashboards or add cache-invalidate hook on re-ingest. Owner: Marta. ETA: 2026-06-20.

3) Long term (quarter roadmap items):
   - Move to typed telemetry contracts and generate ingestion adapters (reduce manual mapping).
   - Evaluate using the Optimize team’s batching recommendations to reduce telemetry noise for high-volume routes.

Decisions made during standup:
- Rollback confirmed for canary v3.4.1; re-deploy blocked until schema sign-off.
- Telemetry schema validation will be a hard blocker for any frontend changes that add or rename top-level keys.
- Add a one-line requirement in the rollout checklist: "telemetry contract approved by ingestion owners".

Incident timeline (concise):
- 03:10 UTC: canary deployed to 5% traffic.
- 03:14 UTC: first missing latency datapoints observed in SLO dashboards.
- 03:20–03:30 UTC: investigation (frontend + ingestion) identifies schema mismatch; rollback initiated.
- 03:35 UTC: rollback completed.
- 03:40 UTC: re-routing metrics to legacy collector; partial re-ingest started.
- 04:40 UTC: initial reprocess finished; dashboards partially restored.

Postmortem notes (to be expanded):
- Contributing factors: lack of mandatory telemetry contract sign-off; silent ingestion drop behavior; dashboard TTL masking re-ingest progress.
- Mitigations: schema validation, pre-rollout synthetic smoke test, dashboard re-ingest indicator.

Communication plan:
- Internal: short incident note to the company tomorrow (Priya). Include timeline and immediate mitigations.
- Customers: no customer-facing incident; product to confirm. If asked, Jordan will provide a canned statement.

Action items (who/what/when):
- Priya: draft telemetry contract doc + internal incident note (ETA 2026-06-15).
- Samir: implement schema validation and alerting for dropped rows (ETA 2026-06-15).
- Marta: add dashboard re-ingest indicator + verify re-ingest completeness (ETA 2026-06-13).
- Ethan: revert open frontend telemetry change in PR 892 and create a feature-flagged version (ETA 2026-06-13).
- Jordan: update rollout checklist and schedule a cross-team sign-off ritual for telemetry changes (ETA 2026-06-19).

Notes-to-self / brainstorming fragments (informal):
- Could we make the aggregator emit a synthetic heartbeat when it sees a new top-level key? That would have tripped earlier.
- Consider a small "telemetry-linter" as a pre-commit step to catch accidental schema changes.
- For big rollouts, maybe switch to a "telemetry mirror" that writes both old + new payload shapes during transition period.

References and links:
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-4212 (canary rollback incident), JIRA-MET-3380 (aggregation schema work)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/892 (frontend telemetry change)
- Playbook: confluence.redwood/console/canary-playbook

Next sync: 2026-06-13 09:30 PT — focus on verification of re-ingest and schema validation progress.

Appendix (raw logs / commands used during investigation):
- samir@ingest: reprocess --from 2026-06-10T03:00Z --to 2026-06-10T05:00Z --verify-checksums
- marta@dash: curl -X POST https://dash-api/ui/cache/invalidate?dashboard=rollout-critical
- ethan@fe: git revert --no-commit 7f4b3c2 (telemetry field addition)

End of notes.
